title: WASSCE Further Maths: Calculus (Differentiation & Integration) - Further Mathematics - Applications of Integration (Trapezium Rule)
subject: Further Mathematics

questions.q: Use the trapezium rule with 4 intervals to estimate $\int_0^2 x^2 dx$.
questions.explain: With 4 intervals from 0 to 2, the width $h = \frac{2-0}{4} = 0.5$. The $x$-values are $0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2$. The corresponding $y$-values ($x^2$) are $0, 0.25, 1, 2.25, 4$. Using the trapezium rule formula $Area \approx \frac{h}{2}[y_0 + y_n + 2(y_1 + y_2 + y_3)]$: $Area \approx \frac{0.5}{2}[0 + 4 + 2(0.25 + 1 + 2.25)] = 0.25[4 + 2(3.5)] = 0.25[11] = 2.75$.

questions.q: Use the trapezium rule with 2 sub-intervals of equal width to estimate the value of $\int_1^3 \frac{1}{x} dx$.
questions.explain: The width of each interval is $h = \frac{3-1}{2} = 1$. The x-values are $1, 2, 3$, with corresponding y-values $1, \frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{3}$. Using the formula $\text{Area} \approx \frac{h}{2} [y_0 + y_n + 2(y_1)]$: Area $\approx \frac{1}{2} [1 + \frac{1}{3} + 2(\frac{1}{2})] = \frac{1}{2}[\frac{4}{3} + 1] = \frac{1}{2}(\frac{7}{3}) = \frac{7}{6}$.
